Record date: 2129-03-27
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 03/27/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Worsening respiratory symptoms, persistent lower extremity edema, and follow-up on anxiety management.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for follow-up approximately five weeks after his last visit. He reports a notable deterioration in his respiratory condition, characterized by increased dyspnea at rest and a persistent cough producing clear sputum. He has been using his albuterol inhaler excessively, now averaging ten times daily, particularly during the night when he experiences nocturnal wheezing.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains pronounced, with Mr. Fairfax rating the discomfort as 9/10. He has adhered to his sodium-restricted diet but has gained an additional 2 pounds since his last visit. The patient expresses significant frustration regarding his ongoing swelling and the associated limitations it imposes on his mobility.
In terms of mental health, Mr. Fairfax indicates that his anxiety levels have escalated, particularly in light of his deteriorating physical health. He reports difficulty concentrating and increased insomnia, with frequent awakenings throughout the night. He has continued his cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions but feels that the current dosage of sertraline may not be sufficient.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + weight gain, + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + increased dyspnea at rest, + nocturnal wheezing, + productive cough, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using ten times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 200 mg daily (no change). 7. Sertraline 150 mg daily (considering increase). 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 82, BP 140/90, RR 28, O2 sat 79% on room air.
General: Elderly male in moderate respiratory distress, appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, marked wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.2, Hgb 10.1, Hct 30.0, Plt 210. 2. BMP: Na 130, K 4.4, Cl 98, CO2 20, BUN 55, Cr 3.2, Glucose 90. 3. BNP: 800 (further elevated). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.8 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory condition has significantly worsened, necessitating a referral to pulmonary medicine for comprehensive management. A nebulized bronchodilator regimen will be initiated to alleviate acute symptoms, and a follow-up spirometry is warranted. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. The serum creatinine has further deteriorated, indicating progressive renal impairment. Nephrology will be consulted urgently for evaluation and management of his renal function, with potential adjustment of his diuretic regimen. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema remains a concern despite ongoing furosemide therapy. Dietary sodium restrictions will be reinforced, and furosemide may require dose adjustment based on nephrology recommendations. Daily weight monitoring continues to be essential. 4. Mental health: Due to increased anxiety and insomnia, an increase in sertraline to 200 mg daily is recommended. A referral to psychiatry for medication management will be expedited to address the worsening mental health symptoms.
Patient education was reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to manage COPD and edema effectively.
